page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, and AVX512_BF16) and cryptographic acceleration via AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. This instance does not include local storage or integrated GPU hardware.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core CPU testing and Geekbench text processing scoring in the top 25%. However, multi-core performance and general computational workloads, such as Passmark CPU and Geekbench multi-core tests, fall within the average range. A significant performance bottleneck is observed in memory bandwidth; while small-block cached reads are average, large-block uncached reads are weak, and large-block uncached writes are poor, falling into the bottom 10% of tested systems. Large-model LLM inference also shows limitations, with prompt processing for a 7B model scoring in the bottom 25%.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c3d-highcpu-8 offers a high-density compute profile with dedicated AMD EPYC resources, making it a viable option for CPU-bound workloads that do not require massive memory footprints. Due to the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and poor uncached memory write bandwidth, it is less suited for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. It is best aligned with workloads such as web serving, text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, and lightweight containerized applications.
